name: trace
purpose: A span waterfall: one row per span of a run (a function invocation, a request through several services), indented under the span it ran inside and drawn as a bar placed against the run's own clock. The rows form a tree grid that expands and collapses, a search narrows them to the spans whose name or service matches, and selecting a row opens its details (service, start, duration, share of the run, outcome message and attributes) under the waterfall. It reads a flat `spans` list with `parentId` links and never fetches anything. With `zoomable`, a minimap under the axis draws the whole run and a window the reader drags or resizes (or moves from the keyboard) to zoom the waterfall into part of it, through `v-model:range`. A span can carry `events` — moments inside it, drawn as markers on its bar and listed in its details — and `highlightSlowest` flags the span that took longest. `highlightCriticalPath` traces the critical path — the chain of work that set the run's end, walked back from the root's end through the child that finished last before each point — and draws a line under each bar along the stretches of that span that lie on it, so the reader sees which work to shorten to make the run faster. The details of a span with children show its self time (its duration less the time its children covered), and of a span on the critical path, its time on that path. The same spans read in three views the reader picks with a `ToggleGroup` in the toolbar, bound to `v-model:view`: `waterfall` (the default: the tree of spans with a bar per row on the run clock), `timeline` (bars only, on one shared time axis: each nesting level is a band, and spans of a level that do not overlap share a lane, so a whole run fits in a few lines) and `tree` (the nesting only, with the start and duration of each span as text instead of a bar). Search, selection and the details are shared by the three views; the zoom applies to the two views with a time axis.
useWhen: Use Trace for the timed span waterfall of one request or invocation; a nested data hierarchy without timing is a Tree.
The test run of a function or the detail of one invocation, to show where the time went.
A request that crossed several services, each with its own span, where the order and the overlap matter.
Next to the run's logs (`log-viewer`), on the same clock.
avoidWhen: A list of log lines with levels → use `log-viewer`.
Durations to compare across many items with no parent/child relation → use `bar-list` or `chart`.
Status history of a service over days → use `tracker`.

In a docs Markdown page or the site's page JSON. Trace is app-only (decision RV-C2-1, rule `azion-ui-content-channels`): it explores one run (expand, search, select a span for its details), so it has no `DocMarkdown` tag and no page JSON entry. A docs page or the site explains where the time went with a `FlowDiagram` or a `Chart`.
related: `log-viewer` — the run's log lines, shown under the trace on the same clock.
`tree` — the same expand and collapse model without the time axis.
`key-value-list` — the facts of the run above the trace.
bestPractices: Pass `start` and `duration` in milliseconds from the start of the run; the axis spans the latest end.
Link children with `parentId`; a span whose parent is missing becomes a root, so a partial trace still renders.
Set `status: 'error'` and a one-line `message` on the span that failed, and on its parents if the failure bubbled up.
Turn on `zoomable` for a run with many short spans next to one long one, so the short ones can be read; bind `v-model:range` when the logs or a chart beside the trace should follow the same window.
Use `events` for moments that have no duration of their own (a cache miss, a retry, the first byte), with `at` on the run's clock; keep the names short, they are listed in the details.

Turn on `highlightCriticalPath` where the question is what to make faster: shortening a span off the path does not shorten the run, shortening one on it does. It reads better than `highlightSlowest` when work runs in parallel, because the longest span is not always the one that held the run up.
Turn on `highlightSlowest` where the question is where the time went; the flag goes to the longest span under the root, never to the root itself, which always spans the run.
Bind `v-model:view` when the reader's choice of view should last: the page can keep it across traces or sessions. Unbound, each trace opens in the waterfall.
Use the timeline view for a run with many spans or a narrow panel, the tree view to read names and durations as text, the waterfall when both the nesting and the timing matter.
Bind `v-model:selected-key` when another view (a request path, a log line) selects the same span.
Name the waterfall after the run (`aria-label="Trace of inv_7f21"`).

props.name: spans
props.doc: Spans of the trace, each `{ id, parentId?, name, service?, icon?, start, duration, status?, message?, attributes? }` in milliseconds.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the waterfall. Empty uses the locale catalog.

props.name: bordered
props.doc: Draws the outer border and radius. Off for a trace inside a card or panel that has its own.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Shows placeholder rows while the spans load; search and selection wait.

props.name: zoomable
props.doc: Shows a minimap under the axis to zoom the waterfall into a window of the run. Supports v-model:range.

props.name: highlightSlowest
props.doc: Flags the span that took longest, other than the root, in its row and its details.

props.name: highlightCriticalPath
props.doc: Draws the critical path of the run under the bars and flags the spans on it in their rows and details.
